messages:
customer-jordan: Hey team — we just had a bad user-facing regression after an autoscale/regional failover. Requests routed from us-east-1 -> eu-west-2 are returning shortened/incoherent completions and some replies include weird tokenization artifacts. Billing looks like tokens are charged normally. Can someone triage?

sara-support: sorry you're seeing this, jordan. Can you paste the request_id and a sample request (with prompt) and the response you got? Also which model you asked for and whether you passed region/route hints?

customer-jordan: request_id: r-0a1b2c3d, workspace: acme-ops. We requested model: redwood-1.2-large, with region=us-east-1 header. Example prompt: "Summarize the following legal clause..." Response starts fine then abruptly jumps to tokenized garbage like "▁ï»¿The clause..." (see attached).

customer-jordan: curl we used:```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Region: us-east-1" -d '{"model":"redwood-1.2-large","prompt":"Summarize..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

sara-support: thanks. I'm checking routing logs. @infra-bot can you pull the routing decision for r-0a1b2c3d and the served model variant?

infra-bot: Routing lookup for r-0a1b2c3d: requested region us-east-1; routed to eu-west-2 failover pool due to transient capacity shortage in us-east-1. Served model: redwood-1.2-small-quant (quantized, small embed config). Tokenizer config id: tk-v2-legacy.

eva-ml: hmm that tokenizer id is incompatible with redwood-1.2-large canonical tokenizer (tk-v3). Small quant variant uses legacy tokenization; that explains garbled output and capability drop.

james-oncall: putting high priority on this. @eva-ml, is the fallback mapping supposed to pick a tokenizer-compatible variant? This looks like a misconfiguration in the fallback table for region routing.

eva-ml: It should. Current policy: when large variant unavailable, fallback_policy -> nearest-compatible variant by arch, but our compability table missed quantized-small-variants mapping to tk-v3. Basically we allowed a size downgrade without enforcing tokenizer version.

sara-support: customer impact: quality drop and some unexpected token sequences. Also note customer reported normal billing — tokens consumed counted against them. We need to confirm whether any outputs violated content policies (they were degraded, not unsafe).

customer-jordan: we saw elevated latency too — p95 jumped from 120ms -> 420ms for those routed requests. Large impact on UX.

james-oncall: reproduction steps for SRE/ML: 1) set region header to us-east-1, 2) force us-east-1 capacity exhaustion via test flag or simulate, 3) send sample prompt (I'll attach). We should see requests routed to eu-west-2 and served by small-quant variant.

eva-ml: quick debug snippet to reproduce locally (internal):```
# simulate request with forced failover header
python repro.py --model redwood-1.2-large --force-failover eu-west-2 --prompt "Summarize the following legal clause..."
```
Expected: should be served by redwood-1.2-large or compatible tokenizer; observed: redwood-1.2-small-quant + tk-v2-legacy -> tokenization drift.

infra-bot: I created an emergency incident: INC-2026-1792. Notifying routing and model-onboard teams.

incidents-bot: Incident INC-2026-1792 created by infra-bot: "Region failover served incompatible variant/tokenizer causing quality regression". Pager notified for oncall rotation.

james-oncall: Immediate mitigation: 1) lock routing to avoid cross-region failover for customer acme-ops (temporary pin to us-east-1), 2) update fallback table to exclude quantized-small-variants without tk-v3 mapping, 3) roll a hotfix to routing policy to check tokenizer compatibility before substituting variants.

sara-support: Jordan — we pinned your workspace to us-east-1 while we patch. You should see new requests back to normal. Can you confirm in ~10 minutes?

customer-jordan: confirming — after pinning p95 back to ~130ms and responses look correct again. Thanks.

eva-ml: root cause summary for postmortem: fallback policy did not verify tokenizer compatibility when selecting substitute model variants during region failover. This allowed a quantized small variant with legacy tokenizer to be selected for a request expecting tk-v3, yielding garbled output and capability regression.

james-oncall: next actions (owner tags): eva-ml -> fix fallback compatibility checks + add unit tests (ETA 24h); infra -> deploy routing policy hotfix and rollout canary (ETA 2h); support -> notify affected customers and offer credits (sara-support). Add regression alert for tokenizer mismatch served in failover.

sara-support: filing follow-up with customer-facing notes and credits proposal. Will loop back when outreach complete. :thumbsup:
